title: Plan: claim-store hygiene — the prompt fix, the cleanup, and the document
body:
**Second push.** The review gate blocked the first correctly: the plan had no `## Summary`, which AGENTS.md states structurally rather than stylistically — *"the plan starts with a `## Summary` the owner can approve from alone"*. It now opens with one, **36 lines against the 40-line ceiling**, carrying every decision the owner could say no to: the asymmetric-recall ruling, what is deliberately not done, and that this costs nothing — no gate change, no required check, no money, no manual step. It ends with the explicit open-questions list (there are none; both Uncertainties are ruled). The body elaborates the Summary and introduces no decision of its own.

The reviewer's two non-blocking points are answered in the document rather than only here. `covers: [R27]` is kept because `coverage.sh` reads that field, and the Open questions section now says plainly that R27 is the requirement this work must not VIOLATE, with the second Uncertainty as where that is shown. The `docs/plans/oracle/` placement is unusual for a plan answering an escape rather than an `OD-<n>`, and is kept because it satisfies that directory's mechanical constraint and the plan needs no oracle authority it does not have.

The plan the previous attempt (#210) did not have. It is cited by nothing yet and governs three slices; the work lands after it, never alongside it.

**Why it exists.** #210 put a document and a data-cleanup script on a `feat/stage-b-extraction-*` branch, which made the `plan` check pass by slug match while the plan in question governs none of it. The review gate blocked it and was right: the decision that actually mattered — where the line falls between a motherboard claim and a graphics-card claim — was never ruled on by anyone. It is ruled on here.

**The HIGH-risk Uncertainty is the owner's, and it is already settled.** The owner ruled in chat on 2026-08-25, twice and unprompted the second time: *"it is way more important to include motherboards than to exclude gpus"* and *"I will accept including gpus by mistake … make sure you are not removing motherboard claims, that is the bigger error."* So the error budget is asymmetric **by instruction**: recall of motherboard claims is the constraint, precision against graphics cards is merely the objective, and a rule that is unsure keeps the claim. The plan requires that to be a mechanical guard in slice 2 with a test that fails if it is loosened — not a note in a docstring.

**A second Uncertainty is answered rather than left implicit:** removing rows from the store does not conflict with R27, because R27 governs the raw model output under `data/claims/batch-<n>/`, which is written before anything parses it and is not touched. The store is derived, the removal is a committed script rather than a hand edit, and nothing is destroyed that cannot be rebuilt.

**Three slices, ordered.** Slice 1 fixes the prompt and lands the test that makes deleting the exclusion go red — ESC-29's ratchet, and it must land first, because cleaning the corpus while the prompt still produces the mess is exactly the shape ESC-29 exists to stop repeating. Slice 2 removes what the defect already produced. Slice 3 documents the store for whoever reads it next.

**Out of scope is stated explicitly:** filtering, ranking and aggregation are Stage C; nothing is re-extracted, so nothing is paid for twice; and the alias list is not touched, because what makes GPU videos reach the corpus is the alias list doing its job correctly.

Ran locally: `plan-lint.sh` — 17 plans parse.
